derived_cause: The settle leg of the round is awaited INSIDE the play call, so the round is closed on the platform before any of it has been presented to the player. In `_rgsSpinReal`, `await endRound(...)` runs at rgsService.ts:801 and `spin()` only resolves at :807, so the `/wallet/end-round` request has already completed by the time the caller receives its `SpinResult` (App.svelte:1422, cited as 1414). Per the platform's own wallet doc that request 'Completes a round, triggering a payout and ending all activity for that round' (docs/stake-engine-live/2026-07-29/rgs_wallet.md:98). Everything a player actually sees happens after that point: the reel animation at App.svelte:1453 (cited as 1445), the wincap dwell at :1485, the Overdrive free-spins presentation at :1537/:1539, and the balance settlement at :1503/:1544. For a triggered round that is 8/12/16 free spins plus retriggers played out against a round the RGS already considers finished. The gate at rgsService.ts:799 does not cause this, it only decides whether the call is made, and against a live RGS it always resolves to `playResp.active`: `OfficialPlayResponse.round` is non-optional (rgsService.ts:200-203) and `_normalisePlay` always sets `round: raw.round` (:642, :654), so `playResp.round` is truthy on every real response and the `winMicros > 0` fallback is dead code; `active` is precisely the flag meaning the round is still open, so the request fires on exactly the rounds whose presentation window it collapses. The compliance consequence is that the platform's disconnect/resume contract can never engage: rgs_wallet.md:26 says the authenticate round 'may represent a currently active or the last completed round. Frontends should continue the round if it remains active', and :118 offers `/bet/event` to track 'in-progress player actions during a round. Useful for resuming gameplay if a player disconnects.' The frontend's own recovery path implements the correct order (sessionRecovery.ts:256 `await present(...)` then :262 `endRound`, with its comment at :253-254 'PRESENT, before settling ... a player who reloaded during a feature is owed the round, not just its number'), but it can only run when `round.active === true` (sessionRecovery.ts:207); after `_rgsSpinReal` has settled, authenticate returns that round as the last COMPLETED round and `recoverSession` takes the `kind: 'none'` branch at :207-211. The TR-099 checkpoint machinery is unreachable in live play for the same reason: `liveBetID` is assigned at App.svelte:1428-1429 from an already-settled round and passed to FreeSpinsPresentation at :1938, while `validateCheckpoint` (sessionRecovery.ts:235) sits inside the active-round branch that can never be entered. The buy path has the identical shape (App.svelte:658). Net effect: the round's active window, which the platform models as the spin-to-settle presentation window (docs/RGS_CONTRACT_REFERENCE.md:43-47), is collapsed to one network round trip, and a live player who reloads mid-Overdrive loses the feature with no resume and no replay while their balance already carries the win.
reasoning:
Spec first, per convention (l.1). The platform's own wallet page is the specification for the round lifecycle: /play 'Initiates a game round and debits the bet amount' (rgs_wallet.md:78), /end-round 'Completes a round, triggering a payout and ending all activity for that round' (:98), authenticate returns a round that is either active or the last completed one and 'Frontends should continue the round if it remains active' (:26), and /bet/event exists to checkpoint 'in-progress player actions during a round ... Useful for resuming gameplay if a player disconnects' (:118). That fixes the round's ACTIVE interval as the presentation interval; docs/RGS_CONTRACT_REFERENCE.md:45-47 states the same thing in the project's own words ('the payout is credited at /end-round, not at /play. This models the spin -> settle animation window').

Against that specification the cited code is read as a sequence. rgsService.ts:778 play -> :801 await endRound -> :805 parse -> :807 return. The await at :801 means the round is closed before the function returns, and the caller does not begin presenting until after it returns: App.svelte:1422 is the await, :1453 is the first frame the player sees, :1537/:1539 is the feature, :1503/:1544 is settlement. So the whole presentation runs outside the round's active window, by construction and not by timing.

LINE-NUMBER NOTE: the record cites App.svelte:1414 and 1445; at HEAD (3047c61) the two lines are 1422 and 1453. Both are shifted by exactly 8 and their separation is unchanged at 31 lines, and the record's own quoted fragment ('const result: Sp') matches line 1422 verbatim, so the citation resolves to `const result: SpinResult = await spin(...)` and `if (gridRef) await gridRef.animateSpin(result.board)`. The file has since grown 8 lines above that point.

The gate on line 799 was checked separately so as not to mistake it for the cause. It is not: `round` is non-optional on OfficialPlayResponse (:200-203) and is always assigned in _normalisePlay (:642, :654), so against any real response the ternary is `playResp.active` and the winMicros fallback is unreachable. That makes the gate the thing that guarantees the call fires on live open rounds, i.e. it widens the exposure rather than creating it.

The consequence was confirmed by reading the module that would have to absorb it. sessionRecovery.ts is the resume path and it is written in the opposite order on purpose (:253-262), which is the strongest in-repo evidence that present-before-settle is the intended contract; and its entry condition is round.active === true (:207), which a round settled at :801 can never satisfy on the next authenticate. The TR-099 checkpoint (App.svelte:1428-1429, :1938; sessionRecovery.ts:235) is gated behind the same branch, so it is dead in live play.

What is derived and what is not: the ordering, the always-true gate, the recovery entry condition and the unreachable checkpoint are all direct reads and are stated as such. The platform docs mirrored in this repository do not contain a sentence explicitly forbidding an early end-round; the breach is derived from the resume contract at rgs_wallet.md:26 and :118 being unsatisfiable once the round is closed, which is a consequence rather than a quoted prohibition. That distinction is recorded per convention (l.7) so no one later quotes a rule that was not written.
